title: What risk costs
description: War-risk premium is the price the market puts on a passage, quoted as a percentage of the ship's hull and machinery value per transit or per period. It is the number an escort service is ultimately sold against, because it is the only maritime risk figure that is already a line item on someone's voyage budget.

how_it_works.basis: Percentage of hull and machinery value, per transit or for a defined period
how_it_works.quoting: Voyage-specific, commonly renewed on seven-day cycles when an area is hot
how_it_works.trigger: The Joint War Committee's listed-areas circular turns a geography into a premium
how_it_works.who_pays: Under most time and voyage charters the charterer bears it, which is why the charterer, not the owner, is often the party with the budget

premiums.note: The peacetime baseline. Everything else in this table is a multiple of it.

open_questions: What does a private armed guard team cost per transit today, and what premium discount does carrying one actually earn? This is the direct price comparison for an escort product and it is missing from this library.
What is the all-in cost of routing round the Cape of Good Hope instead — extra days, bunkers, charter hire, and the working capital tied up in cargo at sea? That delta is the true addressable price.
Do underwriters discount for an escort at all, and who has to certify it? Without a broker willing to write the discount, the value has to come entirely out of the routing saving.
How much of the Red Sea premium is severity and how much is uninsurability of consequence — crew death, total loss, environmental liability?
